stemBlocks.value: A table shows values of a linear function f: x = −2, −1, 0, 1, 2 with f(x) = −5, −2, 1, 4, 7. (a) Determine a function rule for f(x). (b) Calculate f(6). (c) Find the element of the domain whose image is 13.
Think first: The function is linear, so look for the constant step in f(x) as x increases by 1.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p121-q04 from workbook page 121.

solutionSteps.instruction: Find the change in f(x) for each increase of 1 in x.
Read the value of f(x) when x = 0 to get the constant term.
Write the rule and test it on another column.
Solve 3x + 1 = 13 for the input whose image is 13.

strategyBlocks.value: Find the constant difference in f(x) per unit increase in x to get the gradient, read the value at x = 0 for the constant term, then use the rule forwards for f(6) and backwards for the input giving 13.

whyThisWorks.value: A linear function changes by the same amount for every unit step in x, so the constant difference in the table is the gradient. The value at x = 0 is the y-intercept, which is why a table containing x = 0 lets you write the rule with no algebra at all. Part (c) reverses the rule: given the image, solve for the element of the domain that produces it.

commonErrors.misconception: Using the difference between f(x) values without checking that the x values step by 1.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Using the difference between f(x) values without checking that the x values step by 1.

commonErrors.misconception: Reading the constant from the first column instead of from x = 0.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Reading the constant from the first column instead of from x = 0.

commonErrors.misconception: Substituting 13 for x in part (c) instead of setting f(x) = 13.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Substituting 13 for x in part (c) instead of setting f(x) = 13.

examTip.value: Always verify a rule found from a table against a column you did not use — one check rules out an arithmetic slip.
